newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Santos 1st qtr revenue up 22.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Santos 1st qtr revenue up 22.5 pct.

text.p: Oil and gas producer Santos Ltd said on Tuesday its sales revenue rose 22.5 percent to A$181.3 million in the three months to March 31.
Sales volume rose 15 percent in the March quarter, compared with a year ago, to 9.2 million barrels of oil equivalent (BOE), also a record for the quarter, the company said in its quarterly report.
Production volume rose 6.8 percent to 9.6 million BOE.
The results incorporated the activities of all assets acquired from WMC Ltd, effective January 1.
Exploration spending rose 75.8 percent from a year earlier to A$109.5 million. The company said it had a 60 percent success rate from exploration and appraisal wells spudded.

Of total expenditure, A$84.3 million was spent on development projects, reflecting development activity in southwest Queensland associated with new gas contracts, an increased development programme in the South Australian portion of the Cooper/Eromanga Basin, and commencement of the Stag oil field development in the Carnarvon Basin in Westen Australia.
Santos said higher product prices contributed to the result.

Australian dollar prices received for crude oil rose 14.5 percent, naphtha/condensate by 27.6 percent and LPG by 38.5 percent, reflecting higher world prices. However, the effects were partially offset by a stronger Australian dollar.

Gas production rose 14.9 percent to 39.3 petajoules from 32.4 PJ a year earlier. This reflected increased sales to customers in New South Wales and South Australia, ethane concentrate sales for ICI Australia Ltd which started in mid-1996, and production from East Spar off the north west coast of Western Austalia, Santos said.
Crude oil production fell 11.6 percent during the quarter to 1.747 million barrels from 1.976 million a year earlier.

"Approximately 50 percent of the reduction occurred in the Timor Sea as a result of the natural decline of wells and shutdowns due to adverse weather conditions, combined with the cessation of production from the Skua field," Santos said.
"The natural decline of fields in other areas also contributed to this result," it said.
Production from the Banff Early Production System in the U.K. in the first quarter (with no corresponding production a year earlier) provided a small offset to other decreases.
Naphtha/condensate production increased by 6.5 percent to 581,9000 barrels from 546,600.
The full quarter of condensate production from East Spar (92,800 barrels) more than offset the reduced level of production in Queensland. The WMC assets contributed 61,900 barrels of condensate.

LPG production fell 11.5 percent to 62,400 tonnes from 70,500 a year earlier, reflecting decreased production from the Surat Basin/Denison Trough and the South Australian sector of the Cooper/Eromanga Basins.
